title: Car Suspension Spring-Damper System
prompt:
Create a single HTML file that implements a 3D car suspension spring-damper simulation using Three.js.

## Three.js Import (MUST follow exactly)
In the <head>, use this importmap and import via ES Module in <script type="module">:
```html
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
</script>
```

## Scene Setup
- Background color: 0x87CEEB (sky blue).
- PerspectiveCamera at position (8, 6, 12), looking at (0, 1, 0).
- OrbitControls enabled for mouse rotation.
- DirectionalLight at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.5, casting shadows. AmbientLight with intensity 0.4.
- Shadow mapping enabled on the renderer (PCFSoftShadowMap).

## Ground and Terrain
- Create a ground plane (100 x 100) at y=0, color 0x556B2F (dark olive), receiving shadows.
- Generate a bump profile along the z-axis (the car drives along z). The profile is selected by a dropdown (id='select-terrain') with options: 'sine' (sine wave with amplitude 0.3, wavelength 4), 'step' (single step bump of height 0.4 at z=0, width 2), 'random' (Perlin-like random bumps). Render the bump as a narrow raised strip (width 4, centered on the car path) using a BufferGeometry where vertex y-positions follow the profile. The strip must visually show the terrain bumps.

## Car Body (ferrari.glb)
- Load ferrari.glb using GLTFLoader from the path './ferrari.glb'.
- Scale the model to fit roughly a 4m length. Position it so the body is ~0.8m above ground at rest.
- The car body moves forward along +z at a constant speed controlled by slider (id='slider-speed', range 0-20, default 5, label 'Speed m/s'). The car loops: when z > 50, reset to z = -50.

## Spring-Damper Suspension (4 independent units)
- Define 4 wheel positions relative to the car center: front-left (-0.8, 0, 1.4), front-right (0.8, 0, 1.4), rear-left (-0.8, 0, -1.4), rear-right (0.8, 0, -1.4).
- Each suspension unit has: rest length L0 = 0.5m, spring stiffness k (adjustable), damping coefficient c (adjustable), current compression x, compression velocity v.
- At each wheel position, sample the terrain height h_terrain from the bump profile at the wheel's world z-coordinate.
- The wheel bottom sits at h_terrain. The suspension compression is: x = L0 - (carBodyY - h_terrain - wheelRadius). wheelRadius = 0.25.
- Spring force: F_spring = -k * x (restoring). Damper force: F_damper = -c * v (velocity-dependent damping).
- The total vertical force on the car body from all 4 units determines the body's vertical acceleration (mass = 1200 kg). Also compute pitch torque from front/rear force differential and roll torque from left/right differential. Use simplified Euler integration with dt = 1/60.
- Visualize each spring as a zigzag line (yellow) between car body attach point and wheel. The zigzag should compress/extend visually with the spring.
- Visualize each wheel as a dark cylinder (radius 0.25, width 0.2).

## Controls
- Slider id='slider-speed': range 0-20, step 0.5, default 5. Label 'Speed (m/s)'. Controls car forward speed.
- Slider id='slider-stiffness': range 5000-100000, step 1000, default 30000. Label 'Stiffness k (N/m)'. Updates spring constant for all 4 units.
- Slider id='slider-damping': range 500-10000, step 100, default 3000. Label 'Damping c (Ns/m)'. Updates damper coefficient for all 4 units.
- Select dropdown id='select-terrain': options 'sine', 'step', 'random'. Regenerates the terrain strip mesh when changed.
- Button id='btn-reset': Resets car position to z=-20, body at rest height, zero velocities.
- Keyboard: press 'p' to toggle pause (isPaused).

## HUD (id='hud')
- Position: top-left, semi-transparent black background (rgba(0,0,0,0.6)), padding 12px, font: 14px monospace, color white.
- Sub-elements:
  - id='hud-speed': current speed value.
  - id='hud-fl': front-left spring compression in cm.
  - id='hud-fr': front-right spring compression in cm.
  - id='hud-rl': rear-left spring compression in cm.
  - id='hud-rr': rear-right spring compression in cm.
  - id='hud-pitch': pitch angle in degrees.
  - id='hud-roll': roll angle in degrees.

## State Management
Every frame, update window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- frameCount (int): incremented each frame.
- carZ (float): car world z position.
- carBodyY (float): car body y position.
- speed (float): current speed m/s.
- stiffness (float): current k value.
- damping (float): current c value.
- compressionFL (float): front-left compression in meters.
- compressionFR (float): front-right compression in meters.
- compressionRL (float): rear-left compression in meters.
- compressionRR (float): rear-right compression in meters.
- pitchAngle (float): pitch angle in radians.
- rollAngle (float): roll angle in radians.
- terrainType (string): 'sine', 'step', or 'random'.
- suspensionValid (boolean): true when all compressions are finite and within [-0.5, 0.5] range.
- isPaused (boolean): pause state.

## Physics Constraints
- Spring force F = -k * x must produce oscillatory behavior visible when driving over bumps.
- Damping must cause oscillations to decay. Higher c means less oscillation.
- The car body should pitch forward when front wheels hit a bump and roll when one side hits a bump.
- Conservation: total vertical force should keep the car from flying away or sinking through ground.
- When speed=0, the car should settle to rest height with all compressions near zero.
physics_constraints: Spring force: F_spring = -k * x where x is compression from rest length. Damper force: F_damper = -c * v where v is compression velocity. Total body force = sum of 4 spring-damper forces - mg. Euler integration for body position and velocity. Pitch and roll from front/rear and left/right force differentials. Mass = 1200 kg, g = 9.81 m/s^2.
